sections.html:
Fairfield is a shoreline town in Fairfield County, next to Bridgeport, Trumbull, Easton, Weston and Westport. It had 61,512 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 65,300 for 2024. The town covers 31.38 square miles and uses ZIP codes 06824, 06825 and 06828.

Buyers here shop by section rather than by town: Southport, Greenfield Hill, Stratfield, Tunxis Hill, Grasmere, Mill Plain, Holland Hill and the Fairfield Beach area all price differently. Three Metro-North stations (Fairfield-Black Rock, Fairfield and Southport), U.S. 1, Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway mean commuters care how close a house sits to a platform or an on-ramp.

About 5 miles of Long Island Sound coast, five lifeguarded town beaches and several tidal waterways give Fairfield a lot of houses near water. Mill River, Rooster River, Ash Creek, Sasco Brook and the Aspetuck River all run through town, and the Fairfield Beach area has seen many newer homes built close to the sand and downtown.

A waterfront or low-lying street raises questions an inland street never does. Before you set a timeline, work through a short list.

  • Find out whether the lot sits in a mapped flood zone. Your lender or insurer can check.
  • Look at the age of any bulkhead, seawall or septic system.
  • Gather elevation and insurance history, since buyers on low streets ask for both.

The town's building office can tell you what applies to a specific address.

Real estate tax is billed in four installments. The Tax Collector says any bill of $100 or less is due in full with the first installment, and that nobody should ignore a bill: interest keeps building until the bill is paid or the Tax Assessor removes it, and a bill that never arrived is not an excuse for paying late.

Bill typeDue dates
Real estateJuly 1, October 1, January 1, April 1
Motor vehicleJuly 1 each year
Supplemental motor vehicleJanuary 1
Business personal propertyJuly 1 and January 1
Sewer use, bills over $300October 1 and April 1

The town posts the schedule on its tax due dates page.

Appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals. For the 2026 Grand List, your petition has to be in the Assessor's Office by 4:30 pm on Friday, February 19, 2027, and a postmark does not count. The town's appeals page has the form.

Email to assessor@fairfieldct.org is accepted. File one petition per property, attach a copy of the property card for real estate, and have a notarized affidavit ready if someone else will speak for you.

  • A hearing notice is mailed on or before March 1, and hearings run through March.
  • You get 15 minutes, and testimony is sworn and recorded.
  • The Board votes later at a separate meeting.
  • It can raise an assessment as well as lower it, so file only with solid evidence.
  • If you still disagree, you can apply to Superior Court within 60 days of the mailed notice.

The Board has used state law to skip hearings on commercial properties assessed over $1,000,000. Owners of those go straight to court.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax at the closing table
sections.html:
Selling a Fairfield house adds a state filing to the local tax bill. Form OP-236 is the conveyance tax return, and it goes in when the deed is recorded. Either the grantor or the grantor's attorney or agent can sign it. A transfer of $2,000 or more counts as taxable unless an exemption covers it, and the code to use for Fairfield is 051.

Two exemptions come up for stressed owners: a deed given in lieu of foreclosure on the home you live in, and a sale of your residence at a price too low to clear the mortgages and the tax liens ranked ahead of them. The state's conveyance tax page carries the complete list. Your closing agent works out the actual figure for the Fairfield deed.

An open balance does not stop a sale. Whatever is still due gets paid out of your proceeds, so you can list the house or hand it over as-is without writing a check first. The order of work below keeps surprises small.

  1. Call the Tax Collector and find out which quarterly installments are paid and which are open.
  2. Ask whether sewer use is billed on the property. That bill runs on its own October and April calendar.
  3. Pass the figures to your closing attorney or title company so the payoff can be written into the statement.
  4. Pick a closing date with the quarterly calendar in mind. One installment is often partly open when a deed changes hands.
  5. Bring photo ID and any estate papers to the closing if the house was inherited.

If a bill never reached you, still call. The tax and its interest stand even when the mail failed, and the office can read you the balance.

Older houses on small lots, shoreline questions and a four-part tax calendar make up the usual list. A house near the beach can carry deferred maintenance, so many owners order an inspection before they list. An inherited house may sit through several due dates while the estate settles who owns it. If tenants live there, the lease has to be dealt with before closing.

A cash sale skips most of that. The buyer takes the house as it stands, you do not schedule showings or fund repairs, and the title company settles any open tax from the proceeds. Compare that against what repairs and another installment would cost you.

sections.h2: Getting ready for the Assessor's Office
sections.html:
If you plan to appeal before selling, a lower assessment can help the next owner and your own final bills. Pull your property card first and read it line by line. Wrong square footage, an extra bathroom or a finished basement that was never finished are the common errors. Bring photos and any recent sale prices for similar houses on your street.

Keep one folder for the petition, the card, your evidence and the date you filed. If you are not the owner of record, for example an executor, gather the authority papers before the hearing so the 15 minutes goes to the case rather than to paperwork.

faqs.q: When are Fairfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due quarterly on July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in full with the first installment.

faqs.q: What is the Fairfield appeal deadline?
faqs.a: For the 2026 Grand List, petitions must reach the Assessor's Office by 4:30 pm on Friday, February 19, 2027. Postmarks do not count, but email to assessor@fairfieldct.org is allowed.

faqs.q: How long is a Fairfield assessment hearing?
faqs.a: Each hearing is 15 minutes, with sworn and recorded testimony. The Board decides later at a separate meeting and can raise or lower the assessment.

faqs.q: What is Fairfield's town code on the conveyance form?
faqs.a: The code is 051 on Form OP-236, the state conveyance tax return filed when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fairfield house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Your proceeds cover the open balance at closing, so an as-is sale works even when installments are still due.
